accroche: From May 25 to 27, 1968, government, employers, and unions negotiate at Grenelle. The text that comes out, called "accords," was signed by none of the parties.
contenu_vulgarise:
Paris, May 27, 1968, around seven in the morning. The negotiations, begun on May 25, end at the Hôtel du Châtelet, at the Ministry of Labor. The same morning, Georges Séguy, general secretary of the CGT, goes to the Renault plant at Billancourt to present the result. His speech is met with jeers: accounts disagree about their target, some saying they were aimed at Séguy, others at the agreement the rank and file had already rejected.

## A Negotiation, Not a Contract

Around Georges Pompidou, the Prime Minister, gather the delegations of the CGT, the CFDT, Force Ouvrière, the CFTC, the CGC, and the FEN, as well as the employers, the CNPF and representatives of small and medium businesses. The text that results is a "draft agreement protocol." The CGT calls it the "Grenelle statement of findings" ("constat de Grenelle"). It was never signed: no party initialed it or acknowledged it as an agreement. What has since been called the "Grenelle Accords" is therefore a statement of findings, not a contract.

## What the Statement Contained

The minimum wage, the SMIG, was to rise to 3 francs an hour on June 1, 1968. According to Bruno Astarian, this represented a 35% increase in Paris, for about 7% of employees, and was above all a catch-up. In the private sector, wages were to rise by 7% on June 1, then by 3% on October 1, 10% in all. Cornelius Castoriadis, cited by Astarian, calculates that on an annual basis this total rise does not exceed 7.75%. Added to this were the right to form union branches in companies and a commitment to move toward the forty-hour week.

## Rejection by the Rank and File

According to Astarian, the assembly of Billancourt workers had already voted to reject the text and continue the strike before Séguy arrived. According to the accounts Bruno Astarian reports, the proposal to make up for hours lost to the strike provokes the sharpest protests. During the day, other factories (Renault-Cléon, Renault-Le Mans, Berliet, Sud-Aviation, Citroën in Paris) also vote to continue the conflict. For part of the working-class base, the gains obtained were insufficient, notably on pay for strike days.

## The Shift

An unsigned text nevertheless produced effects. The right to form union branches in the company received its legal basis from the law of December 27, 1968, which creates the company union branch "in application of the Grenelle accords." A text no one had signed served as the foothold for a law, voted seven months later.

The expression "Grenelle Accords" tells of a social peace obtained in a weekend. The documents tell something else: a statement of findings that no one signed, that workers rejected, and of which at least one point became law. Should a text no one wanted to sign be called an "accord"?

carte.punch: The "Grenelle Accords" of May 1968: a statement of findings no one signed.
carte.idee: On May 25-27, 1968, government, employers, and unions negotiated. The text, called the "Grenelle Accords," is a draft protocol that was never signed: part of the rank and file rejected it, and the law of December 27, 1968 took up the right to unionize in the company.

quiz.question: Why is the expression "Grenelle Accords" debatable?
choix: Because the negotiations were held at the Élysée and not at the Ministry of Labor
Because the employers had refused to sit at the negotiating table
Because the text that came out of the meetings is a draft protocol that no one signed
Because only the CGT negotiated with the government on those three days
quiz.explication: The document is a draft agreement protocol that the CGT calls the "Grenelle statement of findings": no party signed it. The negotiations took place at the Ministry of Labor and brought together the government, six union organizations, and the employers.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What does the Grenelle statement provide on union rights?
choix: The obligation for every employee to join a union in companies of more than fifty people
The creation of a single union per occupational branch, recognized by the state
The right to form union branches in companies
A ban on unions in companies of fewer than ten employees
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The text commits to the right to form union branches in companies, which the law of December 27, 1968 will take up. The other provisions cited do not match the text.

quiz_supplementaire.question: According to Bruno Astarian, what did the 35% increase in the SMIG in Paris on June 1, 1968 represent?
choix: A 35% rise in all private-sector wages within a year
A rise in the minimum wage in Paris, affecting about 7% of employees
A 35% rise in the pay of all Parisian metalworkers
The doubling of the agricultural minimum wage decided by decree
quiz_supplementaire.explication: According to Astarian, the 35% rise concerned the minimum wage in Paris, affected about 7% of employees, and was above all a catch-up. Private-sector wages were to rise by 7%, then 3%.
